question.text: Dinesh, aged 70, gives a Power of Attorney (POA) to his 17-year-old grandson Rohan to manage his bank accounts and investments. Dinesh's family objects, saying a minor cannot be a donee of POA. Which statement is CORRECT regarding this arrangement?

answer.text: A minor cannot be a donee of POA; the arrangement is invalid and void
A minor can be a donee only for Special POA, not General POA
A minor can be a donee only if a court-appointed guardian co-signs the POA
Under Sec 184 of the Indian Contract Act, a minor can be appointed as a donee (agent) of a POA

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 184 of the Indian Contract Act, a minor can be appointed as a donee (agent) of a Power of Attorney. POA documents are of three broad types — General POA, Special POA, and Special POA for Registration. The Trap: Candidates often assume that because minors cannot enter into contracts as principals, they cannot be agents either. Section 184 specifically permits a minor to act as an agent on behalf of a competent principal. Note: A POA is not compulsorily registrable unless it creates an interest in immovable property, and revocation is governed by the agency provisions of the Indian Contract Act.
